title: Step 1: Hook - The Ground Beneath Us
content: Imagine you are sleeping peacefully in your bed or sitting quietly at your school desk. Suddenly, the furniture starts shaking, the fan swings wildly, and things start falling off the shelves. The solid ground beneath you feels like a shaky bridge! What is happening?

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking
content: Why do you think the Earth, which feels so hard and solid, can suddenly start shaking so violently? What do you think is going on deep underground to cause this?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - The Earth's Puzzle Pieces
content.description: Imagine the Earth's crust is not one single solid shell, but rather made up of giant puzzle pieces called tectonic plates. These plates are always moving very slowly. Sometimes, their edges get stuck together. When they finally break free, they send powerful vibrations through the ground!

title: Step 4: Reveal - Earthquakes
content: This sudden shaking of the ground is called an Earthquake (Bhookamp). It happens when built-up energy inside the Earth is suddenly released, causing the tectonic plates to slip or crack. The point deep inside the Earth where it starts is called the focus, and the point directly above it on the surface is the epicenter.

question: What is the main reason why earthquakes happen?
options: Because of heavy rainfall and floods
Because giant puzzle pieces of the Earth's crust slip and release energy
Because of strong winds above the ground
Because the Earth spins too fast

title: Step 6: Reflection
content: Explain in your own words: If you feel the ground shaking violently, what are the first three things you should do to stay safe? Teach these steps to someone at home.

title: Step 7: Connection
content: Earthquakes are natural disasters that remind us of the powerful forces inside our planet. Understanding earthquakes helps engineers build stronger, earthquake-proof houses and helps us prepare better. For example, the devastating earthquake in Bhuj, Gujarat (2001) taught us many lessons about disaster management and safety.

title: Step 8: Mastery Challenge - Earthquake Drill!
content: Create an 'Earthquake Safety Plan' for your home. Identify the safest spot to hide (like under a strong table) and practice the 'Drop, Cover, and Hold On' drill. Pack a small imaginary emergency bag with essentials you might need.
Students often fear earthquakes. Reassure them that while we cannot stop earthquakes, knowing what to do keeps us safe. Emphasize the 'Drop, Cover, and Hold On' technique in class.

A common misconception is that the ground opens up completely and swallows everything. Clarify that while cracks can form, the main danger is from falling objects and collapsing buildings due to the shaking.
